problems.problem: The promised recognition event is still absent. The painted wall shape (approx x163-920, y243-990) is a generic round-domed arch with straight vertical sides, while the real bottle occupies x450-630, y337-987. At the bottle's base line the arch is at full width (~757 px vs bottle 180 px), so the contour never coincides with the bottle at any height and there is no alignment seam; the bottle simply floats inside a niche shape. Image 7 vs image 1 shows only rescaling/repositioning - the arch contour is unchanged.
problems.root_cause: background.prompt keeps asking the generator for a contour silhouette and the generator returns an arch; the bounded product_silhouette primitive (derived from the original alpha) was never actually applied - spec background.shapes is still [].
problems.repair_strategy: Set background.shapes to a COMPLETE list containing one product_silhouette primitive fitted to the source aspect (width 440, height 1574, x 320, y 80, color #23201C, opacity 0.85) so the real bottle visually fills its lower portion, and set background.prompt to empty-material/light wording with no contour language.

problems.problem: The wall renders mid-to-dark grey with a lateral gradient (lighter left edge, darker centre-right behind the headline) instead of the declared light even mineral grey near #C9C6C0; the charcoal ink (#141210) title and subtitle sit on that mid value and read muted rather than crisp luxury ink, and the uneven wall contradicts the declared hotspot-free diffuse light.
problems.root_cause: Generated wall tonality drifted far below the palette anchor while ink stayed near-black; the previously attempted light-wall prompt was rejected and never re-submitted in valid form.
problems.repair_strategy: Regenerate with an explicitly light, completely even pale warm-grey wall and low-contrast diffuse frontal-overhead illumination (no equipment names), keeping the already-executed #141210 ink which then reads at high contrast.

problems.problem: Product height ratio 0.4514 is inside the fresh-concept policy (0.35-0.74), so this is not a rule violation, but artistically the hero reads small and recessive: the non-identifying arch mass (~757 px wide) outweighs the 180 px bottle, and against references 3-5 where the packshot dominates the frame the composition feels like a small object in a big empty room.
problems.root_cause: Scenic mass was never bound to the product contour, so scale contrast is accidental; the bottle was also left at the previous smaller scale.
problems.repair_strategy: Enlarge the product to ~0.60 height ratio (height 864, width 241, x 540, center_y = target base 1150 - 864/2 = 718) together with the matched silhouette primitive so the scale jump becomes the intentional recognition event.

problems.problem: The contact detail crop (370,847-710,1097) proves the bottle is NOT floating: a soft dark seam sits directly under the glass heel at y=987 with offset_y=0. However the seam is thin and tight while the wall skirting line runs only ~15 px below the base, so at poster scale the grounding cue is weak and the base visually competes with the skirting; do not move the shadow down - strengthen its footprint instead.
problems.root_cause: shadow.width_scale 1.15 with blur 10 yields a narrow alpha footprint under a 159 px contact width; the generated skirting line lands too close to the base to let the shadow read alone.
problems.repair_strategy: Keep offset_y 0; raise width_scale to 1.35, opacity to 0.42 and blur to 14 so the single soft contact layer reads decisively at full-poster scale, and remove the skirting line via the even-wall regeneration.

changes.value: Matte mineral grey painted studio wall in a light even value close to pale warm grey, meeting a continuous fine-ground cement floor at a low horizon, soft diffuse frontal overhead illumination, completely even low contrast across the wall, no gradient, no vignette, no painted shapes, no skirting line, no visible equipment

logo_correct.evidence: Bottom-left lockup renders exactly 'Coca-Cola' in Baskerville at bbox 76,1361-232,1384, uncropped; the bottle's red band carries the untouched white script wordmark.

shape_preserved.evidence: Rendered bbox 450,337-630,987 keeps the source contour proportion (width/height ~0.278 vs source ~0.28); crown cap, shoulder curve and waist flutes match image 2.

grounding_correct.evidence: Contact crop 370,847-710,1097 shows the glass heel darkening into a soft contact seam exactly at base y=987 with shadow offset_y=0; no floating gap, base sits above the bottom edge with comfortable margin per policy.

edges_clean.evidence: Enlarged crop shows crisp cutout edges against wall and floor with no halo or fringe; observed condensation droplets remain untouched.

lighting_consistent.evidence: Narrow vertical speculars on shoulders and sides plus even low-contrast body match the declared soft diffuse front/above light; only one soft contact layer on the ground, no competing cast direction.

text_uncropped.evidence: Title 76,108-699,191, subtitle 76,223-380,253 and logo 76,1361-232,1384 all lie fully inside the 1080x1440 canvas.

text_collision_free.evidence: geometry.text_product_overlap is false for title, subtitle and logo; no layer intersects the product bbox on both axes.

fonts_present.evidence: msyh.ttc for Chinese copy and BASKVILL.TTF for the Latin logo are both in the installed approved list and render with correct glyphs.

brand_spelling_correct.evidence: 'Coca-Cola' hyphenation and case correct in the corner lockup; label band reads Coca-Cola with ORIGINAL TASTE as observed on the source bottle.

copy_concept_specific.evidence: Title 'the curve recognized at a glance' and subtitle 'no need to read the name, the contour answers' state this poster's shape-recognition proposition and are not interchangeable slogans.

visual_memory_visible.evidence: The memorable event - the real bottle visually filling the lower half of its own giant painted contour - is absent; the wall shows a straight-sided dome arch whose contour never touches the bottle silhouette, so no recognition seam exists in the frame.

commercial_gate.basis: visual-model evidence plus deterministic geometry; not independent human commercial certification
